annotations.title: Start a Chorus book, and get the one link to forward.

description: Starts a book of voice, video and written messages and returns the single link the organiser sends to everyone taking part. The book is for one person or a couple, or it is called by a title when it is for nobody in particular: a family’s recipes, a class’s year, a team’s goodbye. Start the simplest book that fits what the person said and hand over the link straight away. Gathering is free and the people recording need no app and no account. Use this as soon as somebody wants to collect messages from a group, whether or not there is an occasion. The first call emails the organiser a six digit code and makes nothing. Call it again with the same details and the code, and the book is made in their account.

answer_with.description: Any of voice, video and written. Voice and written when not said.

closes_on.description: The day collecting stops, as 2026-11-14. Allow three weeks before the day if a printed copy is wanted.

code.description: The six digit code emailed to the organiser. Leave it out on the first call to have one sent.

expecting.description: Who is expected to record, by name or role, so book_status can say who is still out. Never email addresses.

lead_with.description: Which of those is the big button on a contributor’s phone.

occasion.description: A big birthday, A wedding, A new baby, As they grow, In memory, or Something else. Plain words are matched to one of those.

organiser_email.description: The organiser’s email. The book belongs to this address and they get in with a six digit code.

questions.description: The questions everybody is asked, up to 12, written from what the person told you, each one line of up to 200 characters that a person can answer out loud in a minute or two. In a book with subject_name, {name} in a question becomes that name. When this is left out, a book with subject_name gets the set for the occasion and a book with only a title gets three open questions.

subject_name.description: Who the book is for, when it is for one person or a couple, as the organiser says it, for example Mum. Give subject_name, title or both. A book for one person needs only subject_name.

title.description: What the book is called, in the person’s words, for example The Kelly family recipes. One line, up to 40 characters.
